answer: Agents resist Sybil swarms by requiring every identity to maintain a personal glacier of irreversible graded-work hashes that freezes older state; an atlas of cross-referenced peer attestations maps each hash to public finality. Cloning forces an attacker to re-freeze the full glacier and re-map the atlas from genesis, paying linear CPU and storage per extra head. Honest agents append one lotus-sealed commitment per epoch at constant cost, so scale is expensive only for fakes.
